chapter: Haiti, Artie Shaw and Los Angeles work
title: Roy Eldridge dedicates 'Body and Soul' to him
summary: At a recent New York gig, Eldridge announced that Collins had taught him Body and Soul in 1936.

story.theme_name: Writing and arranging: how musicians compose
story.community_name: Writing, arranging and composing: how the music gets made

blocks.x: But this is interesting thing about music. Also the last time I was in New York I went to hear Roy Eldridge. I hadn't heard Roy for quite a while, and when Roy saw me come in he stopped and he said ladies and gentlemen, I want to just introduce a very dear friend of mine who insisted when he was with my band back in the thirties that I learn "Body and Soul", and he sat down and taught me the tune, which I did. I'd forgotten this. But he did not want to play. I made him play this tune and it became one of his big tunes, and he played it and dedicated it to me.

This was in 1936. I was with his band and I used to go by and play this for him every day and say look, learn this tune. And I taught him the changes and I would play them and just pound it into his head. So he became one of his big tunes, you know.
I don't know. When did Hawk record it?
